**The terrain graph editor, rebuilt for composites**

The new terrain generator's graph now works at the level of Gaea and World Machine. Select nodes and press ⌘G to make a composite of them, one node that holds them; double-click it to open it, with a breadcrumb back out, its inputs and outputs as columns at the edges, and expose any setting inside so that every node of it shows it as its own. Massif's Mountain opens read only, and Edit a copy makes it the world's own. Frames take a title, a colour and a note, sit in other frames, fold to their title and move with what they hold. Nodes take a name of their own, can be bypassed (B), snap to the grid, line up and arrange themselves in columns, and copy and paste as JSON, between worlds too. Each kind of socket has its colour and shape, points, lines, footprints, instances and volumes included, and a wire an input cannot take says why and which node to put between them. Apply to map writes everything the Map Output carries in one step you can undo: the ground window by window, so that large maps never have to fit in memory whole, then caves, cave biomes and carved or added volumes, then the villages and their roads, replacing those an earlier Apply laid and keeping those placed by hand; a dialog shows how far it is and Cancel leaves the map as it was. Thumbnails show points, lines, footprints and buildings over the relief, and a volume as its cut. The 3D views gain Objects, which shows or hides the trees, bushes and rocks of the layers, and Density, which colours the land by how many objects its layers will place, with a scale, so that you see how thick each forest will be before exporting. The Terrain side now opens on the Generator workspace, the new Terrain Generator, marked Experimental, and the samples and templates of the home screen open there with their graph and its preview instead of jumping to the World side; the generator of earlier versions stays in the area picker as Classic graph, for older maps.
